text:
R303 — Safe observation contract for the v0.1.43 silent-engine watchdog on Intel Arc B570
Date: 2026-10-12 (Asia/Tokyo)
Scope: repeated read-only safety audit of the immutable curated baseline at HEAD 3141c18 and official pristine v0.1.43 at HEAD 7695859, limited to serve/server.py and serve/telemetry.py plus the retained R300 report. No implementation worktree was read. No source/test/import/build/GPU/service/Git/cleanup operation was performed. This report proposes qualification conditions and fixtures; it records no runtime validation.

Decision

The upstream watchdog can be considered only as a fail-closed, opt-in candidate on the Intel Arc B570 after its activity signals are qualified for that exact engine and device. Until then, do not enable engine termination from “low CPU + low I/O + GPU not busy.” Only a fresh, valid, device-matched positive-idle observation can permit a kill decision; missing, malformed, stale, exceptional, reset or ambiguous GPU evidence means observe/warn and leave the engine alive. Preserve the existing generous engine-silence limit as a separate bound.

Source facts relevant to adaptation

The R300 audit established that the immutable curated baseline has no equivalent frozen-engine watchdog; its existing silence handling is not the same behavior. This review does not repeat that omission audit. The upstream pinned source defines STRATA_ENGINE_STALL_S with a 90 s default (zero disables it), a 0.5 CPU-second tolerance and a 1 MiB I/O-byte tolerance. It samples process CPU time and cumulative read+write bytes, and checks only while a generation is silent. If the activity read returns None, it schedules no later check. However, upstream’s engine_frozen comparison accepts any delta at or below the thresholds, including a negative reset/decrease, without an explicit type, finiteness, monotonicity or process-identity check.

Upstream’s GPU veto at server.py around 3204–3207 reads telemetry snapshot gpu_util and evaluates (value or 0) >= 10. That folds missing/None/zero into not-busy. In multi-GPU telemetry, the snapshot’s aggregate utilization is the mean of whichever per-card values are readable; missing cards are omitted. A mean is unsuitable as proof that every engine-selected card is idle.

The curated Xe telemetry uses Intel xe-driver DRM fdinfo and Level Zero sysman, not an Intel equivalent of NVML global engine utilization. Its _XeGpu._busy computes render/compute cycles from process fdinfo on the configured PCI device. It returns 0 when no DRM client records are found, None when clients exist but no usable advancing total-cycle interval is available, and a percentage when interval counters can be formed. The periodic Telemetry sampler runs about once per second. snapshot() returns the latest value but no sample timestamp. Thus the existing telemetry interface cannot establish freshness, and a zero can mean “no client record observed,” not positive evidence that the target engine is idle. Its activity can also include same-user processes, not only the Strata engine PID. The Arc B570 case is Intel; an earlier R301 report’s “NVIDIA B570” wording was incorrect.

Required decision contract

1. Keep observation and termination separate. Enable an observation mode first; it may log request age, validated CPU/I/O deltas, GPU sample age/PCI identity/status and whether a watchdog decision would have fired, but it must never stop the engine. Runtime validation on the actual B570 must show the telemetry contract is reliable before an opt-in termination mode is considered. Default behavior on unknown evidence is no kill.
2. Scope every decision to one engine generation and one active request. Bind samples to the engine object/process identity (PID plus create time or equivalent process-start identity), selected PCI BDF(s), and request/generation ID. Reset the activity baseline when a protocol line arrives, a request starts/ends, cancellation/STOP begins, SAVE/RESTORE/session work starts, the engine restarts, or the process identity changes. Never carry a quiet-window baseline across those boundaries or PID reuse.
3. Accept CPU and I/O counters only as finite, non-boolean, nonnegative numeric values of the expected shape. Require both CPU and I/O counters and a positive monotonic interval. Deltas must be >= 0; a decrease, NaN/Inf, unsupported field, exception, permission error, dead/reused process, or implausible interval invalidates the pair and reseeds/observes. Never reinterpret invalid or reset deltas as zero. Preserve the upstream 0.5 CPU-second and 1 MiB thresholds only as initial candidate tolerances, not as B570 qualification.
4. GPU activity is a three-state signal: BUSY, IDLE, UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN includes None, absent key, exception, non-finite/out-of-range percentage, missing device, BDF mismatch, stale sample, no trustworthy client attribution, non-advancing or reset counters, and incomplete selected-device coverage. BUSY vetoes killing. UNKNOWN also vetoes killing. Only IDLE can participate in a kill decision, and IDLE must be positively established for the exact engine-selected GPU(s), not inferred from absent telemetry or a same-user/card aggregate.
5. Add a sampler monotonic timestamp and selected PCI identity to the watchdog-facing observation record (without changing unrelated Monitor display semantics). A sample is fresh only within a documented bound; given the current ~1 s sampler interval, use 3 s as a preliminary cap and require consecutive fresh samples covering the entire quiet window with no gap above that cap. Any gap, source error, invalid value or identity mismatch changes the window to UNKNOWN. A single latest snapshot cannot establish 90 s of idle.
6. For multi-GPU or split execution, use engine-selected devices only. Require a valid sample for each selected device; any BUSY device vetoes, and any UNKNOWN device vetoes. Do not use the telemetry UI’s mean or its partial-card average to prove idle. Unselected cards are irrelevant; unrelated same-user GPU activity may conservatively veto but must not be mistaken for the engine’s own progress.
7. Termination is eligible only after the silence interval has reached the configured stall threshold, the same engine/request remains active, valid CPU+I/O counter pairs establish below-threshold nonnegative deltas for the full interval, and fresh device-specific GPU observations establish IDLE throughout that same interval. If any condition fails, do not kill; retain the ordinary silence timeout and issue at most one diagnostic warning per request/window. GPU work or host work restarts the comparison window from the new baseline.
8. Long prefill is an explicit protected case. PP/progress or any protocol line resets the silent-window state. If a single chunk can run longer than the stall threshold, its potentially long device work must remain protected by fresh BUSY telemetry; if B570 telemetry cannot prove that route active for the full interval, the freeze watchdog cannot safely terminate during that chunk. Do not lower the separate engine-silence timeout to make the watchdog appear responsive. If no documented upper bound or trustworthy activity state exists for a long in-flight kernel, report “unqualified/observe only.”
9. Cancellation/STOP is not a frozen-engine sample. On cancellation, suppress the watchdog and use the existing bounded STOP/DONE drain contract. Do not kill because STOP temporarily leaves CPU and I/O counters quiet; let the explicit STOP completion deadline classify failure. Clear state before another request, before restart, and when control/session operations change the engine phase.
10. Counter and telemetry handling must be non-throwing at the server boundary. Any provider exception becomes UNKNOWN and a bounded diagnostic, never an inference of idle and never an API/server crash.

Meaningful CPU-only mock qualification

Use a deterministic fake clock and fake process object; do not use real sleep, psutil sampling, a model, or GPU. The mock process must expose PID/create-time identity, cpu_times and io_counters; inject sequences and exceptions. The GPU provider must return the explicit BUSY/IDLE/UNKNOWN tri-state plus sample time, PCI BDF and per-device readings. Exercise the actual watchdog decision path with these cases:

- Low CPU and low I/O with fresh B570 GPU BUSY: observe, never kill.
- Low CPU and low I/O with GPU UNKNOWN because missing/None/exception/stale/BDF mismatch/no client or non-advancing fdinfo: observe, never kill. Include the current telemetry’s no-clients -> 0 and clients-with-no-usable-span -> None cases; neither is accepted as IDLE without target-process attribution.
- Low CPU and low I/O with a valid, fresh, target-device IDLE sequence spanning the whole threshold: only this case may make the kill decision eligible, after the full delay and same request/process identity checks.
- CPU-only progress above tolerance and I/O-only progress above tolerance independently veto; reads and writes each count. Threshold equality and just-over-threshold cases have explicit expected behavior.
- Missing psutil/import error, process disappearance/access denied, CPU-only or I/O-only None, exceptions, NaN, +Inf/-Inf, negative values, booleans, wrong tuple length/types, counter decrease/reset, and invalid elapsed time all invalidate/reseed and never kill. A reset between samples cannot look like zero activity.
- Freshness gaps, stale-but-last-value-idle, bad device identity, one selected card missing among several, an active card hidden by an average, and an unselected active card are tested separately. For selected cards, any active device vetoes; any missing/unknown selected card vetoes.
- A long PP interval beyond the configured watchdog window with simulated GPU BUSY stays alive; PP/protocol progress resets the window. A progress line followed by idle is evaluated only from its new baseline.
- Cancellation/STOP, DONE, SAVE/RESTORE, request completion/new request, engine restart and PID reuse clear or suppress the old window. Quiet STOP drain uses its own deadline and never triggers the activity kill path.
- Keep an observation-only run mode and assert it emits the would-kill diagnostic without invoking kill across every invalid/unknown fixture. Assert kill is invoked at most once only for the fully qualified explicit-idle fixture.

These are proposed fixtures, not tests executed in this audit. They should be run CPU-only before any device validation. A real B570 qualification then separately verifies process attribution, fdinfo counter semantics across active long-prefill and truly idle/fault cases, sample freshness under service load, engine-selected PCI mapping, and that zero/None/provider failures behave as expected. Until that evidence exists, the safe adaptation state is observation-only; a valid-looking Monitor gauge alone is not enough to authorize termination.

Evidence inspected

- Official pristine v0.1.43 serve/server.py at supplied HEAD 7695859: timeout/watchdog constants around 230–263; generation silent wait and state reset around 1640–1690; _activity and _stall_check around 1751–1787; GPU callback wiring around 3204–3207.
- Official pristine v0.1.43 serve/telemetry.py: 1 Hz sampler, GPU aggregation, timestamp-free snapshot, and NVML/AMD telemetry implementation.
- Immutable curated baseline HEAD 3141c18 serve/server.py and serve/telemetry.py: Xe fdinfo/sysman telemetry implementation and no watchdog equivalent.
- R300 retained audit: research-current-v0143-functional-import-audit-round300-v1.txt. It records the existing omission and the distinction from the baseline’s general engine-silence behavior; no attempt was made here to re-state its broader import findings.

No source or test was changed and no watchdog was executed.
